title: Todos
steps: Open Chores. Todos are checkboxes, with chips for when they're due ("Overdue 1d" in orange, "Today" in blue, then "Tomorrow", a weekday, or a date) and how they repeat ("↻ weekly"). Done todos are muted and struck through.

Move the cursor onto a todo (j and k, or click its text): that line shows its raw markdown, `- [ ] … due:2026-… every:…`, so you edit real text. Vim motions like w, e, f and x only ever meet real characters. Move off it and the checkbox and chips come back.
Click Book a dentist appointment's checkbox: it's checked off, and the cursor stays where it was, in normal mode. Click again to reopen it.
Click Water the plants' checkbox: it shows checked for a moment, then stays open with its due date moved on 3 days, on the same line. Nothing piles up.
Show history of this note: that change reads "Completed 'Water the plants' (due …)", by you.
Put the cursor on a todo and press ⌘Enter (Ctrl+Enter off a Mac), or gx in normal mode: the same toggle from the keyboard.
Click a chip: the cursor goes to its text, which shows raw, ready to change the date.

⌘⇧P, Show todos: every open todo in every note, under Overdue, Today, Upcoming and No date, with the same checkboxes and chips. Check one off there: it's written to its note as a change by you. Click a title to jump to its line.
Write your own: `- [ ] Call the bank due:2026-12-01 every:month`. `every:` takes day, weekday, week, month or year, with an optional count, like `every:2weeks`.
